To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tRNAGln anticodon is recognized by the enzyme through the phosphate-sugar interactions of the nucleotides in the acceptor stem.
the phosphate-sugar moieties of three nucleotides in tRNA Gln are important for the enzyme to recognize the tRNA as Gln.

1) The phosphate-sugar backbone of nucleotides in the D-loop and T-stem regions of the tRNA Gln molecule interact with the enzyme, 2) these interactions are sequence dependent and contribute to tRNA recognition and identity, 3) these interactions help communicate enzyme binding at the anticodon end of the tRNAGln to the catalytic center, 4) the D-loop and anticodon loop regions of tRNAGlu interact with the enzyme at different sites
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of aminoacylation of tRNA.
the mechanism of protein synthesis.
the mechanism by which a specific enzyme recognizes and catalyzes the formation of an aminoacyl-tRNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anticodon is the primary determinant of the identity of the tRNA.
phosphate-sugar backbone recognition of tRNA Gln by E. coli glutaminyl- tRNA synthetase is an important component of acceptor identity.

the phosphate-sugar backbones of the nucleotides in tRNA Gln are involved in tRNA Gli acceptor identity, and that these interactions help communicate the identity of the anticodon end of tRNA Gln to the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tRNAs are more than just a string of nucleotides.
the phosphate-sugar moieties of tRNA are important for recognition by the enzyme, and that these moieties are important in the overall structure of tRNA.
the phosphate-sugar backbones of tRNA Gln interact with the enzyme to contribute to tRNA acceptor identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interactions of the phosphate-sugar backbones of tRNA with the enzyme are critical for tRNA identity.
tRNA Gln recognition is a composite of sequence-dependent interactions at the anticodon and acceptor ends of the tRNA.
tRNA Gli acceptor identity is not a simple consequence of the anticodon.
